name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on *all* PRs for two weeks. This lets us measure real impact without risking disruption, catching false negatives early when they hurt most. The trade-off is temporary noise in PR comments—acceptable because we prioritize quality over speed. Done when the lead confirms the decision and PR-Agent is deployed in shadow mode.

name: Gauge
text: Shadow mode won’t catch PR-Agent’s worst flaw: false negatives. It normalizes bad changes by never blocking them, so the real risk is undiscovered regressions slipping into production. Instead, run PR-Agent in *parallel mode* for two weeks—it flags issues but lets humans override, exposing both false positives *and* false negatives without sacrificing safety. Done when the lead confirms the artifact (parallel mode logs) and the team agrees the trade-off (extra human review time) is worth the risk reduction.

name: Overhaul
text: Run the parallel test only on PRs from *new contributors*—they’re less likely to spot PR-Agent’s mistakes, so this cuts risk where it matters most. This keeps the test cheaper by reducing the volume of false positives we must manually review.
